method: Each claim checked against the retrieved structured abstract of the 2018 NHFA/CSANZ guideline. Only the abstract was retrieved; the full guideline was not. Firecrawl declines health.qld.gov.au at provider level.
source_coverage: S1 structured abstract only. Full guideline text NOT retrieved. Thinnest source base in this set, stated in the guideline itself.

claims.claim: Recommendations graded on strength of evidence and likely absolute benefit versus harm; additional considerations given as practice points
claims.source_text: These clinical practice guidelines focus on the diagnosis and management of HF with recommendations that have been graded on the strength of evidence and the likely absolute benefit versus harm. Additional considerations are presented as practice points.

claims.claim: Blood pressure and lipid lowering decrease the risk of developing HF
claims.source_text: Blood pressure and lipid lowering decrease the risk of developing HF.

claims.claim: SGLT2 inhibitors decrease the risk of HF hospitalisation in patients with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease
claims.source_text: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors decrease the risk of HF hospitalisation in patients with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

claims.claim: An echocardiogram is recommended if HF is suspected or newly diagnosed
claims.source_text: An echocardiogram is recommended if HF is suspected or newly diagnosed.

claims.claim: If echocardiogram cannot be arranged timely, plasma B-type natriuretic peptides improve diagnostic accuracy
claims.source_text: If an echocardiogram cannot be arranged in a timely fashion, measurement of plasma B-type natriuretic peptides improves diagnostic accuracy.

claims.claim: ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists improve outcomes in HF with reduced LVEF
claims.source_text: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, beta-blockers and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists improve outcomes in patients with HF associated with a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction.

claims.claim: Additional options in selected patients with persistent HFrEF: switch ACEi to ARNI, ivabradine, ICD, CRT, atrial fibrillation ablation
claims.source_text: Additional treatment options in selected patients with persistent HF associated with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction include switching the angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor to an angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor; ivabradine; implantable cardioverter defibrillators; cardiac resynchronisation therapy; and atrial fibrillation ablation.

claims.claim: Multidisciplinary HF disease management facilitates implementation of evidence-based HF therapies
claims.source_text: Multidisciplinary HF disease management facilitates the implementation of evidence-based HF therapies.

claims.claim: Clinicians should consider models of care that optimise medication titration, e.g. nurse-led titration
claims.source_text: Clinicians should also consider models of care that optimise medication titration (eg, nurse-led titration).

claims.claim: Designed for systematic integration into HF care including ongoing audit and feedback
claims.source_text: These guidelines have been designed to facilitate the systematic integration of recommendations into HF care. This should include ongoing audit and feedback

claims.claim: 2025 meta-analysis of 11 RCTs, 32,654 participants, HFrEF; SGLT2 inhibitors most effective in Asian patients for composite of HF hospitalisation, cardiovascular death and all-cause mortality, RR 0.61 (95% CI 0.49-0.75)
claims.source_text: We included 11 RCTs involving 32,654 participants from Asian and white populations. In Asian patients, SGLT2 inhibitors (risk ratio [RR] 0.61; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.49-0.75) were the most effective in reducing the composite endpoi[nt] ... The primary outcome was a composite endpoint of hospitalization of HF, cardiovascular death, and all-cause mortality.

claims.claim: No newer Australian heart failure guideline exists
claims.note: PubMed searched for Australian/CSANZ heart failure guidelines 2021-2026; results were audit and implementation studies, not a replacement guideline. Absence of evidence, recorded as such rather than asserted.

claims.claim: Current place of SGLT2 inhibitors in HFrEF irrespective of diabetes
claims.note: S1 predates this evidence and S2 is a single population-stratified meta-analysis. The divergence is recorded; no recommendation is written.
